anim.hidratacion: Hydration: 400 g of pellets + 600 ml of water. The pellets soak up the water and break down into sawdust.
anim.puno: Fist test: squeeze a handful hard. Good: 1 or 2 drops come out.
anim.pasteurizacion: Pasteurization: if you pour in boiling water and leave it uncovered, it cools into the mold zone within minutes. Boiling for 15–20 min, or covering and insulating, keeps the heat in.
anim.past.hold: Boil 15–20 min or cover and insulate
anim.inoculacion: Inoculation: layers of substrate and spawn. Spawn is 10 % of the wet weight: 100 g per kilo (⅔ measuring cup).
anim.sellado: Oxygen: with a loose knot the bag breathes (air in, CO2 out). With a tight knot it goes stiff and smells sour.
anim.sell.squeeze: Squeeze: air should come out through the knot
anim.perforaciones: Holes: 4 to 6 pinholes in the top half of the bag.
anim.colonizacion: Colonization: the white growth spreads from each bit of spawn until it covers the bag (about 14–21 days). If a green spot appears, throw the bag away.
anim.fructificacion: Fruiting and harvest: open the bag, the pins come out, and you cut them before the caps open all the way.
anim.materiales: Know your materials: pellets look like cat kibble; grain spawn is rice or sorghum with a white, cottony coat; use hydrated lime, never quicklime.

calc.title: Amounts calculator
calc.intro: Enter how much dry substrate you have. Everything is recalculated for your amount, in grams and in kitchen measures.
calc.type.pellet: Pellets or powder (sawdust, spent coffee grounds)
calc.boilOpen: I'll boil the water uncovered (add 5 % for evaporation)
calc.potLiters: Liters of water in the pot (for fiber)
calc.spawnMin: Minimum that still works, but slower (3–5 %)
calc.stoveText: Boil fully submerged 15–20 min with the lime, or pour, cover and insulate at least 1 hour. Let it cool covered overnight (8–12 h).
calc.microText: {n} batch(es) of {min} min, at most 1 kg each, in a microwave-safe container with a loose lid; stir halfway. Let it cool covered overnight (8–12 h).
calc.fiberText: Boil the fiber submerged in the lime water for 1 hour. Let it cool covered overnight (8–12 h) and drain until it stops dripping.
calc.invalid: Enter a number between 50 and 20 000 grams.
calc.noScale: No scale? The pellet sack and the spawn pack have the weight printed. Loose pellets: 1 level measuring cup ≈ {g} g.
tests.title: Tests to check you're on track
tests.fist.title: Fist test (moisture)
tests.fist.body: Squeeze a handful of hydrated substrate hard. Good: 1 or 2 drops come out. A stream means too much water: drain or squeeze. Nothing comes out and it crumbles dry: add water one tablespoon at a time and test again.
tests.air.title: Air test (oxygen)
tests.air.body: After closing the bag, squeeze it with your hand. Air should come out through the neck of the knot. If nothing comes out, the knot is too tight: loosen it or make 4 to 6 pinholes in the top half.
alerts.title: Warning signs
alerts.green: Green or black spots: contamination by other molds. Throw the bag away closed, far from the others. Don't try to save it and don't eat it.
alerts.sour: Sour or fermented smell: bacteria from too much water or not enough air. Check the fist test and the air test on your next bag.
alerts.nogrowth: The spawn isn't growing and there are no spots: the substrate is too dry, the spawn is old, or it was left in the sun.
alerts.warranty: Contamination in the first 8 days: the spawn probably arrived contaminated. If you bought it on Mercado Libre, claim the guarantee with photos.
safety.title: Safety
safety.lime: Use only hydrated lime (calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2, also called slaked lime or builder's lime). Never quicklime (calcium oxide, CaO): it heats up on its own with water and can boil and splatter. At the hardware store, read the bag: if it says "quicklime", "calcium oxide" or "CaO", don't use it.
safety.noLime: If you only have quicklime or no lime at all: don't use it; use sustained heat pasteurization instead (boil fully under water for 15–20 min, or cover and insulate for at least 1 hour).
safety.water: Never pour boiling water straight into a thin plastic bag: it can melt or burst and burn you. Use a pot or a heat-resistant container.
safety.ppe: Minimum protection: washed hands, face mask and gloves when inoculating; gloves and glasses when measuring and mixing lime, because the dust can damage your eyes. If lime gets in your eyes, rinse with clean water for 15 minutes and seek medical care.
safety.eat: Don't eat mushrooms with green or black spots or a sour smell.
safety.toxic: Worried it might be toxic? Pleurotus (oyster mushrooms) grown from bought spawn in a bag with no contamination are edible. Be suspicious if you see odd colors, spots, a sour smell, or if you don't know what spawn you used. Eat them cooked.

a.title: Start here
steps: Get spawn (the mushroom's "seed") of Pleurotus ostreatus: white grains like rice covered in a cottony layer. Keep it in the fridge (1–4 °C).
Get substrate (the material it grows on): sawdust pellets, preferably hardwood (not pine), or agave-bagasse pellets. They look like light-brown cat kibble.
Get hydrated lime (slaked or builder's lime), never quicklime. A 400 g pellet bag needs 6 g.
Have ready: measuring cup and spoons, a heat-resistant pot, a thick plastic bag, a spray bottle, face mask, gloves and glasses.
a.test: Open the spawn: it should smell like fresh mushrooms and look white, with no green or black spots.
a.ifWrong: If it arrives with spots or gets contaminated in the first 8 days, claim the guarantee from the seller.

b.title: Prepare and inoculate
steps: For every 400 g of pellets (2½ measuring cups) use 600 ml of water (one 600 ml bottle) with 6 g of hydrated lime (2½ level measuring teaspoons).
Pasteurize (kill competing microbes): boil the substrate submerged 15–20 min, or pour the boiling water, cover and insulate at least 1 hour. In a pot, not in the bag.
Let it cool covered overnight (8–12 hours).
Inoculate (mix the spawn into the substrate): 10 % of the wet weight, 100 g per kilo (⅔ measuring cup, or 1/5 of a 500 g pack). Washed hands, mask and gloves.
Close with a loose knot or make 4–6 pinholes near the top. Never tie it tight.
b.test: Fist test: 1 or 2 drops. Air test: when you squeeze the bag, air comes out through the knot.
b.ifWrong: Stream of water: drain it. Dry and powdery: add water a little at a time. No air comes out: loosen the knot.

c.title: Incubation
steps: Keep the bag at 24–28 °C, in the dark and out of drafts (closet, box, under the bed).
Don't open it. Check it every 2 or 3 days without moving it much.
Between day 5 and 7 you should see white, cottony growth spreading from the grains.
To colonize (for the white to cover everything) takes 14 to 21 days.
c.test: By day 7 there's white growth coming out of each grain.
c.ifWrong: Green or black spots: throw the bag away closed. Sour smell: too much water or not enough air.

d.title: Getting the mushrooms to fruit
steps: When the bag is all white, make one or more cuts with clean scissors.
Put it in indirect light, out of direct sun and strong drafts, with fresh air.
Keep the air humid: mist the walls of the space 2 or 3 times a day, not the bag.
Pins (baby mushrooms) appear in 1 to 2 weeks.
d.test: In a few days, small white or gray bumps appear at the cuts.
d.ifWrong: If the pins dry out, it needs more humidity. If they come out with long stems and small caps, they need more fresh air.

e.title: Harvest
steps: Harvest while the edge of the cap is still curled down, before it opens all the way (about 25–35 days after inoculation).
Cut at the base with a clean knife or scissors.
Keep misting; you'll get 2 or 3 harvests, about one every 2 weeks.
When it stops producing, use the substrate as compost or animal feed.
e.test: The mushroom smells fresh, with no spots or sour smell.
e.ifWrong: If it has green or black spots or a sour smell, don't eat it.

f.title: Troubleshooting
steps: Green or black spots: other molds. Throw the bag away closed.
Sour smell: bacteria from too much water or not enough air.
Not growing and no spots: too dry, old spawn, or left in the sun.
Contaminated in the first 8 days: claim the guarantee from the seller.
f.test: Compare your bag with the colonization animation.
f.ifWrong: If you're not sure, upload a photo to the assistant or ask at the workshop.
